# jsonstor-couchbase

> Home: [http://jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com)
>
> Version: 0.1.0

### Documents are stored in a Couchbase bucket.

Overview
---------------------------------------------------------------------

`jsonstor` defines one interface for working with a document store and implements it
  for a variety of database products and file formats. The interface is the same whichever
  adapter is underneath, so the storage a project uses becomes a configuration decision
  rather than a structural one.

This package is one such adapter. Documents are stored in a Couchbase bucket.

***It carries no database driver.*** The server is reached over HTTP with the runtime's
  own `fetch`, so this package adds nothing to a project beyond `jsonstor` and `jsongin`.

See [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) for the interface,
  and [jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com) for the documentation.

Getting Started
---------------------------------------------------------------------

```bash
npm install --save @liquicode/jsonstor-couchbase
```

```js
const jsonstor = require( '@liquicode/jsonstor' )();
jsonstor.LoadPlugin( require( '@liquicode/jsonstor-couchbase' ) );

let storage = jsonstor.GetStorage( 'jsonstor-couchbase', {
	Server: '...',
	Port: 8093,
	Encrypt: false,
	BucketName: '...',
	CollectionName: '...',
	PrimaryKey: "_id",
	PrimaryKeyMutable: false,
	UserName: "",
	Password: "",
} );
```

Versions
---------------------------------------------------------------------

This package answers to more than one name. Pass any of these to `GetStorage()`;
  a name which is not listed is refused.

| Name | Dialect it uses | Measured against |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | its own | 5.0 |
| `jsonstor-couchbase` | `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | - |
| `jsonstor-couchbase-v5` | `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | - |
| `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.1` | `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | - |
| `jsonstor-couchbase-v6` | `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | - |
| `jsonstor-couchbase-v6.6` | `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | - |
| `jsonstor-couchbase-v7` | `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | - |
| `jsonstor-couchbase-v8` | `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | - |
| `jsonstor-couchbase-v8.0` | `jsonstor-couchbase-v5.0` | 8.0 |

A name with its own dialect was measured against that server version and covers every
  later one up to the next such name. The rest resolve to one of those. The bare name
  follows the newest dialect this package carries, which is what most callers want.

A name whose dialect your server cannot serve is refused on the first operation, naming
  the version you asked for and the one the server needs.

Settings
---------------------------------------------------------------------

| Setting | Required | Default | Description |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `Server` | ***Yes*** | - | The name or address of the Couchbase server. |
| `Port` | No | `8093` | The query service port. This adapter speaks to the query service and to nothing else, so no other port is needed. |
| `Encrypt` | No | `false` | Reach the query service over `https` rather than `http`. There is no `TrustServerCertificate` beside it, because this adapter has no driver except the global `fetch`, which offers no supported way to relax certificate verification. |
| `BucketName` | ***Yes*** | - | The bucket this storage reads and writes. It must already exist; this adapter never creates one. See the notes. |
| `CollectionName` | ***Yes*** | - | The key range within the bucket which is this collection. It cannot contain a colon. See the notes. |
| `PrimaryKey` | No | `"_id"` | The document field which is the identifier. `String()` of its value becomes the Couchbase document key. `IdField` is the former spelling and still works. |
| `PrimaryKeyMutable` | No | `false` | Allow an update or a replacement to change the identifier. Off by default, so an operation which would move it is refused by name rather than silently discarded. |
| `UserName` | No | `""` | The user to connect as. Empty means none. |
| `Password` | No | `""` | That user's password. Empty means none. |

Peculiarities
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- ***This adapter installs no database driver, and that is a measurement rather than a preference.*** Couchbase is the first target in this family where the driver and the driverless path are not the same wire: the `couchbase` SDK reaches a key/value service on port 11210 which `fetch` cannot reach at all. So the question was what that service buys, and it was timed. ***It buys about 5 ms per by-key round trip***, for 74 MB and a native addon. Everything else is a tie, including the duplicate-key refusal the primary key contract needs. Its one structural advantage - `at_plus`, which waits only for your own mutation to be indexed - was measured at ***199.90 ms against `request_plus`'s 200.27***, because the indexer publishes a snapshot every 200 ms and no client can be faster than the next one.
- ***A bucket is not a collection, and this is the only adapter here where the server's own container was turned down.*** `jsonstor-couchdb` makes a database a collection and `jsonstor-elasticsearch` makes an index one, because both are cheap to create and to drop. A Couchbase bucket is allocated a RAM quota, is created by an administrator over a management port this adapter never opens, and is capped in number by the edition - so a library which spent one per collection would exhaust a cluster at ten. Couchbase's *own* collections could not be it either: they arrived in 7.0, and this package's floor is 5.0.
- ***So the bucket is the container and a collection is a key range inside it.*** Every document key begins `<CollectionName>::`, and the range ends at the next character up - which is `jsonstor-leveldb`'s construction in characters a Couchbase key can legibly carry. One bucket holds as many collections as you like, and `DropStorage` removes exactly this collection's documents and no neighbour's.
  - ***A range and not a `LIKE`, which is a measurement.*** The obvious rendering is `META().id LIKE "name::%"`, and it was measured *returning a neighbour's documents*: a collection named `a%b` matches the key `axxb::1`, because `%` is a `LIKE` metacharacter. A range compares whole strings and has nothing to escape.
  - ***A colon in a collection name is refused***, which is what makes the range exact rather than nearly exact. Without that rule a collection named `aa:` would write keys which sort inside `aa`'s range.
- ***The bucket needs a primary index, and this adapter creates one if it can.*** The Couchbase query service refuses an unindexed keyspace rather than scanning it, which is a class of failure no other adapter here has. The index is created on the first *write* and never on a read - a read against a bucket nobody has written to is an empty collection, and creating an index to answer a `Count()` would make a question change the thing it asks about.
- ***The document is stored at the top level, and here it has to be.*** This is the exact mirror of `jsonstor-elasticsearch`, which cannot avoid a payload because Elasticsearch reserves `_id`. A criteria is translated into a `WHERE` clause naming the document's own paths, and that clause is opaque to the adapter - so there is nothing which could prefix a payload into it. Nothing is reserved here, so the identifier field keeps its own name and its own type in the document, beside a key holding `String()` of it.
- ***`jsonstor_sequence` is reserved, and this adapter is the family's most exposed to that.*** Insertion order is recorded in a field of that name at the top level of the stored document; it is written on every write and taken off on every read, so a caller's own field of that name does not survive. ***A criteria which mentions it is not pushed down at all***, because it would be decided by the server against a field the answer does not have.
- ***What comes back is exactly what went in.*** Couchbase coerces nothing on the way in and reorders nothing: a field holding the string `"10"` comes back a string, an absent field stays apart from one holding null, and an object keeps its field order. ***That is why so much of this translation is exact*** - `N1qlExpression` is the only translator in this family which reports `Residual: null` as a matter of course, because it is the only one whose target shares jsongin's value model. `IS MISSING`, `IS NULL` and `IS NOT VALUED` answer three different questions, which is what `$exists` and `$type` need and no SQL engine here can provide.
- ***Every statement whose predicate resolves through the index asks for read-your-writes.*** The query service reads a secondary index the data service updates asynchronously, so a default query answers from whatever the index happens to hold - and a run which forgets this reads back nothing it just wrote. ***It is not a rule about reading***: a `DELETE ... WHERE` names its rows through the same index, and forgetting it there leaves documents behind.
- ***A lookup by the identifier costs no index and no wait.*** `USE KEYS` reaches the data service directly, so a read by the primary key skips both the index and the 200 ms the snapshot cadence would cost. Every other criteria pays that once per query, never once per document.
- ***A collection reads back in the order it was written***, and the server sorts it. Use `FindMany2` with a `Sort` when you need a different order.

Storage Interface
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Every adapter implements the same functions, and they are documented once:
  [Storage Interface](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com/#/guides/Storage-Interface.md).

***The operator list is not repeated here.*** A criteria, a projection, and an update are
  the engine's, and the list changes whenever the engine gains an operator - a copy in this
  file could only ever be out of date. See the
  [Operator Reference](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin/blob/main/docs/guides/Operator-Reference.md).
